title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
臣交爲有道而媟嫚之不施接爲有禮而傲惰之不
作猶見藹藹吉人於我乎奮庸䕫䕫髦士於我乎效
用此君臣之相感猶物類之相應也故又以爲梧桐
萋萋而菶菶則鳳凰雝雝而喈喈吾王之於賢才將
何以爲禮乎夫車所以載也今吾王之車則既庶且
多而卑非不衆矣馬所以乘也今吾王之馬則既閑
且馳而馬非不習矣其意若曰以是車馬而待彼賢
才亦何厭其多哉是必疊見於詩之章可也而我矢
詩之章則不多焉維以繼王之聲而已爾是必屢形
===
於詩之言可也而我矢詩之言則不富焉特以遂王
之歌而已爾然則待賢之事雖不明於賡歌之間而
勉其待賢之意實已深於賡歌之表若康公者何其
善於戒君也歟嗟夫天下之所可樂者莫如治之時
而所可慮者亦莫如治之時何也蓋治之時以三光
則得其明以四時則得其序以庶類則得其所是固
可樂也然天地盈虛與時消息而謂治可以保其常
治乎此虞廷所以有臯陶之賡歌而周家所以有召
公之卷阿也
punctuated: 臣，交爲有道而媟嫚之不施，接爲有禮而傲惰之不作，猶見藹藹吉人於我乎奮庸，䕫䕫髦士於我乎效用。此君臣之相感，猶物類之相應也。故又以爲梧桐萋萋而菶菶，則鳳凰雝雝而喈喈，吾王之於賢才，將何以爲禮乎？夫車，所以載也，今吾王之車則既庶且多，而卑非不衆矣；馬，所以乘也，今吾王之馬則既閑且馳，而馬非不習矣。其意若曰：以是車馬而待彼賢才，亦何厭其多哉？是必疊見於詩之章可也，而我矢詩之章則不多焉，維以繼王之聲而已爾；是必屢形於詩之言可也，而我矢詩之言則不富焉，特以遂王之歌而已爾。然則待賢之事，雖不明於賡歌之間，而勉其待賢之意，實已深於賡歌之表。若康公者，何其善於戒君也歟！嗟夫！天下之所可樂者，莫如治之時；而所可慮者，亦莫如治之時。何也？蓋治之時，以三光則得其明，以四時則得其序，以庶類則得其所，是固可樂也；然天地盈虛，與時消息，而謂治可以保其常治乎？此虞廷所以有臯陶之賡歌，而周家所以有召公之《卷阿》也。
translation_en: …his ministers: when he associates with them according to the Way, without showing disrespect or familiarity, and receives them with propriety, without giving rise to arrogance or indolence, then one will likewise see the numerous admirable men exerting themselves in our service, and the reverent and eminent scholars rendering their efforts to us. This mutual responsiveness between ruler and minister is just like the mutual resonance among things of the same kind in nature. Therefore, he further considers that since the parasol trees are luxuriant and flourishing, and the phoenixes sing in harmony and unison, wherewith shall our King show courtesy to worthy talents? Now, carriages are for carrying; today our King's carriages are both numerous and plentiful—it is not that carriages [? 卑] are not abundant! Horses are for riding; today our King's horses are both well-trained and swift—it is not that the horses are not well-broken! His meaning is as if to say: in using these carriages and horses to treat those worthy talents, how could one ever tire of having too many? This ought surely to be shown repeatedly in the stanzas of the ode; yet the stanzas of the ode I set forth are not many, serving only to continue the King's melodies and nothing more. This ought surely to take form time and again in the words of the ode; yet the words of the ode I set forth are not copious, serving merely to complete the King's song and nothing more. Thus, although the matter of treating the worthy with courtesy is not explicitly stated within the responsive song itself, the intent of urging him to treat the worthy with courtesy is in fact already deeply embedded beyond the words of the responsive song. Someone like Duke Kang (Kang Gong 康公)—how skillful he was at admonishing his sovereign! Alas! Among the things in the world in which one may rejoice, none compares to a time of good order; yet among the things about which one must feel concern, none compares to a time of good order either. Why is this? Because in a time of good order, as for the three luminaries—sun, moon, and stars—they attain their brightness; as for the four seasons, they attain their proper sequence; and as for the multitude of living things, they attain their proper place. This is certainly cause for rejoicing. Yet the waxing and waning of Heaven and Earth ebb and flow with time—can one say that good order can be guaranteed to remain forever in good order? This is why in the court of Yu (虞) there was the responsive song of Gao Yao (臯陶), and why in the House of Zhou (周) there was the "Juan'e" (卷阿, Curving Slope) ode of the Duke of Shao (Shao Gong 召公).

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
春秋
荊人來聘〔莊公二十三年〕荊伐鄭　公會齊人宋人
救鄭〔莊公二十八年〕遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕
王寅
考試官教諭馮　〔批此作責楚義嚴詞正得旨〕
考試官教諭鄭　〔批題本平易作者多昧遠交近攻內安外〕
〔攘之旨此篇不泛不略可取〕
遠交近攻者外夷之術內安外攘者伯主之功觀可
見荊楚之強非齊桓不能抑也春秋得不備書之哉
===
且夫楚以熊繹之裔嘗懷窺伺中國之志一旦謂鄭
為南北必爭之國魯為秉禮人望之邦圖中國莫先
於攻鄭欲攻鄭莫先於交魯於是首遣介使將命為
聘魯之舉繼遣子元將兵為伐鄭之行其聘魯也人
徒見玉帛煌煌交錯於兩觀之間而不知其心已包
藏乎伐鄭之禍其伐鄭也人徒見車馬彭彭肆暴於
鄭郊之邦而不知其機已胚胎於聘魯之時遠交我
魯近攻一鄭楚人之術何其狡耶幸而齊桓任中國
之伯慨然有安夏攘夷之心意謂不安內圖無以宗
punctuated:
《春秋》

「荊人來聘」〔莊公二十三年〕、「荊伐鄭，公會齊人、宋人救鄭」〔莊公二十八年〕、「遂伐楚」〔僖公四年〕。

王寅

考試官教諭馮〔批：此作責楚，義嚴詞正，得旨。〕
考試官教諭鄭〔批：題本平易，作者多昧遠交近攻、內安外攘之旨，此篇不泛不略，可取。〕

遠交近攻者，外夷之術；內安外攘者，伯主之功。觀可見荊楚之強，非齊桓不能抑也，《春秋》得不備書之哉？且夫楚以熊繹之裔，嘗懷窺伺中國之志。一旦謂鄭為南北必爭之國，魯為秉禮人望之邦，圖中國莫先於攻鄭，欲攻鄭莫先於交魯。於是首遣介使將命，為聘魯之舉；繼遣子元將兵，為伐鄭之行。其聘魯也，人徒見玉帛煌煌，交錯於兩觀之間，而不知其心已包藏乎伐鄭之禍；其伐鄭也，人徒見車馬彭彭，肆暴於鄭郊之邦，而不知其機已胚胎於聘魯之時。遠交我魯，近攻一鄭，楚人之術，何其狡耶！幸而齊桓任中國之伯，慨然有安夏攘夷之心，意謂不安內圖，無以宗…
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"Men of Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiry" [twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang]; "Jing attacked Zheng; the Duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to rescue Zheng" [twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang]; "Thereupon they attacked Chu" [fourth year of Duke Xi].

Wang Yin 王寅

Examiner, Instructor Feng 馮 [comment: This essay censures Chu with stern principle and upright diction, grasping the main purport.]
Examiner, Instructor Zheng 鄭 [comment: The topic is inherently straightforward, yet most writers are blind to the themes of allying with the distant while attacking the near, and pacifying the interior while repelling the exterior. This piece is neither vague nor sketchy, and is worthy of selection.]

To ally with the distant while attacking the near is the stratagem of outer barbarians; to pacify the interior while repelling the exterior is the achievement of a hegemon. From viewing this [?], one can see that the might of Jing-Chu could not have been curbed by anyone other than Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals not record it in full?

Moreover, Chu, as the descendant of Xiong Yi 熊繹, had long harbored ambitions of spying upon and coveting the Central States. Once it reckoned that Zheng was a state over which north and south must contend, and that Lu was a state that upheld ritual and commanded popular esteem, it held that in plotting against the Central States nothing took precedence over attacking Zheng, and in wishing to attack Zheng nothing took precedence over befriending Lu. Thereupon it first dispatched an envoy to convey its command in an act of friendly inquiry to Lu, and subsequently dispatched Ziyuan 子元 to lead troops in an expedition to attack Zheng. In its mission of friendly inquiry to Lu, people merely saw the resplendent jade and silk crossing back and forth between the twin watchtowers, not knowing that in its heart it already harbored the calamity of attacking Zheng. In its attack on Zheng, people merely saw the numerous chariots and horses wreaking violence in the suburban territories of Zheng, not knowing that the mechanism had already been conceived at the time of the mission to Lu. Allying afar with our Lu while attacking nearby Zheng—how狡 (cunning) was the stratagem of the men of Chu! Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi assumed the hegemony of the Central States and resolutely possessed the mind to pacify the Xia and repel the barbarians, reckoning that without pacifying internal schemes [?], there would be no means to rally the allegiance of…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
諸侯不攘外則何以弭外患安內必先於救鄭攘外
必先於伐楚於是首因鄭人告急則師三國之師以
救之繼因楚復虐鄭則会八國之兵以伐之其救鄭
也人徒知楚師夜遁鄭免桐丘之奔而不知由夫齊
桓能明同惡相恤之義也其伐楚也人徒知文告一
脩楚遣納欵之使而不知由夫齊桓能伸脣齒捷伐
之威也內安中國外攘強夷桓公之功何其偉耶春
秋書荊人來聘於荊伐鄭之上于以見楚人懷詐譲
之術書齊人救鄭於遂伐楚之上于以見齊桓著安
===
攘之功懋故曰遠交近攻者外夷之術內安外攘者
伯主之功省此也抑考之荊人聘魯而卒有伐鄭之
師其與楚樹聘魯而遂有厥貉之次同一遠交近攻
之術爾然伐鄭之舉猶幸齊桓躬率諸侯而成安夏
攘夷之功以遏其暴横憑陵之勢厥貉之後特惜晉
靈徒委諸大夫而講新城外楚之盟亦何以杜楚人
闚伯中國之志哉噫五伯桓公爲盛而晉靈不與良
有以也
公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子盟于
punctuated:
諸侯；不攘外，則何以弭外患？安內必先於救鄭，攘外必先於伐楚。於是首因鄭人告急，則師三國之師以救之；繼因楚復虐鄭，則会八國之兵以伐之。其救鄭也，人徒知楚師夜遁，鄭免桐丘之奔，而不知由夫齊桓能明同惡相恤之義也；其伐楚也，人徒知文告一脩，楚遣納欵之使，而不知由夫齊桓能伸脣齒捷伐之威也。內安中國，外攘強夷，桓公之功何其偉耶！《春秋》書「荊人來聘」於「荊伐鄭」之上，于以見楚人懷詐譲之術；書「齊人救鄭」於「遂伐楚」之上，于以見齊桓著安攘之功懋。故曰：遠交近攻者，外夷之術；內安外攘者，伯主之功，省此也。抑考之，荊人聘魯而卒有伐鄭之師，其與楚樹聘魯而遂有厥貉之次，同一遠交近攻之術爾。然伐鄭之舉，猶幸齊桓躬率諸侯，而成安夏攘夷之功，以遏其暴横憑陵之勢；厥貉之後，特惜晉靈徒委諸大夫，而講新城外楚之盟，亦何以杜楚人闚伯中國之志哉？噫！五伯桓公爲盛，而晉靈不與，良有以也。
公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子盟于
translation_en:
… the feudal lords; without repelling the outside, how could one quell external threats? Pacifying the interior had to begin with rescuing Zheng, and repelling the outside had to begin with attacking Chu. Therefore, first, when the people of Zheng reported their crisis, he led [師, sc. 帥] the armies of three states to rescue them; subsequently, because Chu again ravaged Zheng, he assembled the troops of eight states to attack it. In his rescue of Zheng, people merely know that the Chu army fled by night and Zheng escaped having to flee to Tongqiu, without knowing that this came about because Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan 齊桓) was able to make clear the righteous duty of mutual sympathy against a common enemy. In his campaign against Chu, people merely know that once the diplomatic proclamation was set forth, Chu sent an envoy to offer submission, without knowing that this came about because Duke Huan of Qi was able to extend the awe of swift punitive expeditions in defense of closely interdependent states. Pacifying the Central States within and repelling the powerful barbarians without—how magnificent were the achievements of Duke Huan! The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records "Men of Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiries" above "Jing attacked Zheng," thereby showing that the people of Chu harbored schemes of deceit [詐譲, sc. 詐諼]; it records "Men of Qi rescued Zheng" above "and thereupon attacked Chu," thereby showing that Duke Huan of Qi manifested great merit in pacifying and repelling. Thus when it is said that befriending distant states while attacking nearby ones is the stratagem of outer barbarians, whereas pacifying the interior and repelling the outside is the achievement of a hegemon, it refers to [省, sc. 皆] this. Moreover, if we examine it further: that the men of Jing sent a mission of friendly inquiries to Lu and ended up launching an army to attack Zheng, and that椒 [樹, sc. 椒] of Chu sent a mission of friendly inquiries to Lu and thereupon encamped at Juemo, were one and the same stratagem of befriending distant states while attacking nearby ones. Yet in the campaign against Zheng, it was still fortunate that Duke Huan of Qi personally led the feudal lords and accomplished the work of pacifying the Xia and repelling the barbarians, so as to check their violent, unbridled, and encroaching momentum; whereas after Juemo, it is particularly regrettable that Duke Ling of Jin (Jin Ling 晉靈) merely delegated matters to the great officers to negotiate the covenant at Xincheng excluding Chu—how could that suffice to cut off the Chu people's ambition of spying on the hegemony of the Central States? Alas! Among the Five Hegemons, Duke Huan was the most flourishing, while Duke Ling of Jin is not counted among them; there is truly good reason for this!

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
踐土　公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯陳子
莒子邾子秦人于温〔僖公二十八年〕秦人晉人圍鄭
〔僖公三十年〕狄圍衛　衛遷于帝丘〔僖公三十一年〕
張附翼
考試官教諭馮　批〔此作體認明白必熟於麟經者〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔場中作者多不知晉文之報怨行私此篇獨出其心術之微非淺學所能到者〕
敵者可責乎以見晉文之伯始則不能脩德以懷鄭
貳國從伯而私於復怨者可譏外夷猾夏而私於縱
===
終則不能卻狄以安衛春秋得不備書之乎且夫鄭
以懿親之邦嘗堅事楚之志今也因晉文城濮之繼
伯乃幡然改轍而從晉踐土有盟六飛下臨鄭伯嘗
用平禮以傳王于温有會群后咸集鄭伯又嘗偕列
國以聽命鄭之從伯可謂勤矣文公獨不許其自新
乎夫何懷出亡過鄭之私責其無厚贈將迎之禮既
合諸國大夫以謀之復偕秦人之師以圍之社其出
入之路問以無禮之由大之字小果如是乎春秋上
書踐土之盟于温之會下書秦晉圍鄭者于以見晉
punctuated:
踐土。公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、陳子、莒子、邾子、秦人于温〔僖公二十八年〕。秦人、晉人圍鄭〔僖公三十年〕。狄圍衛。衛遷于帝丘〔僖公三十一年〕。
張附翼
考試官教諭馮　批〔此作體認明白，必熟於《麟經》者。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔場中作者多不知晉文之報怨行私，此篇獨出其心術之微，非淺學所能到者。〕
敵者，可責乎？以見晉文之伯，始則不能脩德以懷鄭，貳國從伯而私於復怨者可譏；外夷猾夏而私於縱終則不能卻狄以安衛，《春秋》得不備書之乎？且夫鄭以懿親之邦，嘗堅事楚之志，今也因晉文城濮之繼伯，乃幡然改轍而從晉。踐土有盟，六飛下臨，鄭伯嘗用平禮以傳王；于温有會，群后咸集，鄭伯又嘗偕列國以聽命。鄭之從伯，可謂勤矣，文公獨不許其自新乎？夫何懷出亡過鄭之私，責其無厚贈將迎之禮，既合諸國大夫以謀之，復偕秦人之師以圍之，社其出入之路，問以無禮之由，大之字小，果如是乎？《春秋》上書「踐土之盟」、「于温之會」，下書「秦晉圍鄭」者，于以見晉
translation_en:
…at Jiantu. The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Chen, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and a representative of Qin at Wen [twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi]. The people of Qin and the people of Jin besieged Zheng [thirtieth year of Duke Xi]. The Di besieged Wei. Wei moved its capital to Diqiu [thirty-first year of Duke Xi].

Zhang Fuyi

Examiner and Instructor Feng comments: [This essay shows a clear comprehension; its author must be thoroughly versed in the Unicorn Classic (Spring and Autumn Annals).]
Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: [Most candidates in the examination hall did not recognize how Duke Wen of Jin avenged personal grievances and acted out of selfish motives. This essay alone brings out the subtleties of his inner intentions—something shallow scholarship could never attain.]

[Note: the first two columns of the essay are transposed in the woodblock print:] When a formerly vacillating state follows the hegemon, yet he indulges in personal vengeance, he deserves censure; when foreign barbarians throw the central states into disorder, yet he privately lets the enemy go, is he not to be blamed? Thus we see that in his hegemony, Duke Wen of Jin at first could not cultivate virtue to win over Zheng, and in the end could not repel the Di to bring security to Wei. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals not record these events in full?

Moreover, Zheng, though a state of close royal kinship, had once held fast to its resolve to serve Chu. Now, because Duke Wen of Jin succeeded to the hegemony at Chengpu, Zheng suddenly changed its course and followed Jin. At the covenant of Jiantu, when the royal carriage with its six-horse team descended to attend, the Earl of Zheng assisted the King using the rites of King Ping's time. At the meeting at Wen, when all the feudal lords gathered together, the Earl of Zheng again joined the various states in awaiting commands. Zheng's allegiance to the hegemon may truly be called diligent! Would Duke Wen alone not allow it to renew itself? Why then did he harbor private resentment from when he passed through Zheng during his exile, blaming it for failing to offer generous gifts and proper rites of welcome and farewell? Having first assembled the great officers of the various states to plot against it, he then joined the armies of Qin to besiege it, blocking [?; 社 for 杜] its paths of entry and exit and calling it to account for its lack of courtesy. Is this truly how a great state cherishes a small one? Above, the Spring and Autumn Annals records the "covenant at Jiantu" and the "meeting at Wen," and below it records "Qin and Jin besieged Zheng," thereby showing that Duke [Wen] of Jin…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
文私於復怨而失懷遠招携之道也若夫狄以夷醜
之邦嘗逞猾夏之志令也伺晉伯之業衰率醜類以
圍衛荷氈被毛橫行於康叔之邦陳師鞠旅環攻乎
北州之國衛之被圍可謂急矣晉文獨無拯念之心
乎夫何懷過衛不禮之釁念居狄日久之恩坐視衛
國之受兵不啻秦越之肥瘠卒使衛之人民有塗炭
之苦衛之宗社有帝丘之遷同惡相恤果如是乎春
秋上書狄圍衛下書衛遷于帝丘者所以責晉文私
於縱敵而失方伯連率之職也抑考五伯莫盛於桓
===
文然考其行事而文終非桓匹何耶是故鄭逃齊盟
桓公仗義而為新城之圍非若晉文挾私怨以圍鄭
也衛被狄難桓公恤患而有楚丘之城非若晉文之
懷私恵以縱狄也噫齊桓公正而不譎晉文公譎而
不正觀之於此為尤信
禮記
淳熬煎醢加于陸稲上沃之以膏曰淳熬淳毋
煎醢加于黍食上沃之以膏曰淳毋
陳俊
punctuated:
文私於復怨，而失懷遠招携之道也。若夫狄以夷醜之邦，嘗逞猾夏之志；令也伺晉伯之業衰，率醜類以圍衛。荷氈被毛，橫行於康叔之邦；陳師鞠旅，環攻乎北州之國。衛之被圍，可謂急矣，晉文獨無拯念之心乎？夫何懷過衛不禮之釁，念居狄日久之恩，坐視衛國之受兵，不啻秦越之肥瘠，卒使衛之人民有塗炭之苦，衛之宗社有帝丘之遷。同惡相恤，果如是乎？《春秋》上書「狄圍衛」，下書「衛遷于帝丘」者，所以責晉文私於縱敵，而失方伯連率之職也。抑考五伯莫盛於桓、文，然考其行事，而文終非桓匹，何耶？是故鄭逃齊盟，桓公仗義而為新城之圍，非若晉文挾私怨以圍鄭也；衛被狄難，桓公恤患而有楚丘之城，非若晉文之懷私恵以縱狄也。噫！「齊桓公正而不譎，晉文公譎而不正」，觀之於此，為尤信。

禮記
「淳熬：煎醢加于陸稲上，沃之以膏，曰淳熬。淳毋：煎醢加于黍食上，沃之以膏，曰淳毋。」
陳俊
translation_en:
… Duke Wen of Jin indulged his private desire for vengeance and lost the way of cherishing the distant and winning over the estranged. As for the Di, being a state of loathsome barbarians, they had previously given rein to their ambition of disturbing the Chinese states; now [reading 今 for 令], watching for a decline in the hegemonic enterprise of Jin, they led their vile kind to besiege Wei. Carrying felt and wearing furs, they ran rampant in the state of Kangshu; marshaling armies and addressing troops, they encircled and attacked the state of the northern region. The siege of Wei could be called an emergency—did Duke Wen of Jin alone have no heart to rescue and care for them? Why then did he harbor the grievance of having been treated discourteously when passing through Wei, and remember the favor of having resided among the Di for a long time, sitting by and watching the state of Wei suffer attack with no more concern than a man of Qin has for the leanness or fatness of a man of Yue? In the end, he caused the people of Wei to suffer the misery of mire and charcoal, and the ancestral temples and altars of Wei to undergo the relocation to Diqiu. Is mutual sympathy in the face of a common threat really like this? That the Spring and Autumn Annals first records "The Di besieged Wei" and below records "Wei relocated to Diqiu" is to reprove Duke Wen of Jin for privately indulging the enemy and failing in his duty as a regional earl and leader of states. Moreover, if we examine the Five Hegemons, none were more flourishing than Dukes Huan and Wen; yet if we examine their deeds, Wen was ultimately no match for Huan—why is that? Thus, when Zheng fled the covenant of Qi, Duke Huan upheld righteousness and undertook the siege of Xincheng, unlike Duke Wen of Jin, who harbored a private grudge in besieging Zheng; when Wei suffered the calamity of the Di, Duke Huan pitied their distress and walled Chuqiu, unlike Duke Wen of Jin, who cherished a private favor in giving free rein to the Di. Alas! "Duke Huan of Qi was upright and not crafty; Duke Wen of Jin was crafty and not upright"—looking at it in light of this, the saying is especially credible.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Chun'ao (richly anointed rice): fry meat sauce, place it over upland rice, and drench it with fat; this is called chun'ao. Chunmu (its counterpart): fry meat sauce, place it over glutinous millet, and drench it with fat; this is called chunmu."
Chen Jun 陳俊

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭馮　批此題知養老之珍具而詞理簡明
有僅見此篇
考試官教諭鄭　批淳熬淳毋先王養老之珍也非作得之
觀先王養老之珍饌而制之必極其佳也盖稻黍之
飯加煎醢非不美也養老之用又皆沃之以膏豈不
極其佳而為珍羞之品也哉内則之記謂夫先王養
老非特愛之以敬而已必有淳熬之珍以充其口非
特行之以禮而已必有淳毋之珍以供其饌謂之淳
熬沃淳煎熬為之膳也先王以淳熬之膳而養老果
===
何以制之必也用陸地之稻為之本焉煎肉為醢加
之于稻飯之上非不美也恐其味薄或更以牛羊之
膏而沃之是之謂淳熬也曰淳熬非八珍之一而何
以此而養夫老者則氣體由之而强焉謂之淳毋法
象淳熬為之膳也先王以淳毋之膳而養老抑何以
制之必也用芬芳之黍為之主焉煎肉為醢加之于
黍食之上亦非不美也恐其未佳或更以雞犬之膏
而和之是之謂淳毋也曰淳毋非八珍之二而何以
此而養夫老者則血氣由之而盛焉吁古人於養老
punctuated:
考試官教諭馮　批：此題知養老之珍具，而詞理簡明，有僅見此篇。
考試官教諭鄭　批：淳熬、淳毋，先王養老之珍也，非作得之。

觀先王養老之珍饌，而制之必極其佳也。盖稻、黍之飯，加煎醢非不美也；養老之用，又皆沃之以膏，豈不極其佳而為珍羞之品也哉！《内則》之記謂夫先王養老，非特愛之以敬而已，必有淳熬之珍以充其口；非特行之以禮而已，必有淳毋之珍以供其饌。謂之「淳熬」，沃淳煎熬為之膳也。先王以淳熬之膳而養老，果何以制之？必也用陸地之稻為之本焉，煎肉為醢，加之于稻飯之上，非不美也；恐其味薄，或更以牛羊之膏而沃之，是之謂「淳熬」也。曰「淳熬」，非八珍之一而何？以此而養夫老者，則氣體由之而强焉。謂之「淳毋」，法象淳熬為之膳也。先王以淳毋之膳而養老，抑何以制之？必也用芬芳之黍為之主焉，煎肉為醢，加之于黍食之上，亦非不美也；恐其未佳，或更以雞犬之膏而和之，是之謂「淳毋」也。曰「淳毋」，非八珍之二而何？以此而養夫老者，則血氣由之而盛焉。吁！古人於養老
translation_en:
Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: On this topic, the candidate understands the delicacies prepared for nourishing the aged, and his wording and reasoning are concise and clear—rarely seen except in this essay.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: "Richly drizzled" (chun'ao) and "imitation rich" (chunmu) were the former kings' delicacies for nourishing the aged; one could not have attained this without [true understanding / proper composition] [?].

Observing the fine delicacies with which the former kings nourished the aged, we see that their preparation necessarily reached the utmost excellence. For cooked rice and broomcorn millet topped with fried meat-sauce are by no means untasty; yet when used for nourishing the aged, they were further drizzled with melted fat. How could they not reach the utmost excellence and become items of rare delicacy!

The record in the "Pattern of the Family" (Neize) chapter states that in nourishing the aged, the former kings did not merely love them with reverence, but necessarily had the delicacy of "richly drizzled" (chun'ao) to fill their mouths; they did not merely treat them according to ritual, but necessarily had the delicacy of "imitation rich" (chunmu) to supply their table.

When it is called "richly drizzled" (chun'ao), it is a dish made by richly drizzling and frying. When the former kings nourished the aged with the dish of "richly drizzled," how indeed did they prepare it? Necessarily, they used upland rice as its base. Frying meat to make a sauce and placing it atop the cooked rice is by no means untasty; yet fearing its flavor might be thin, they would further drizzle it with the fat of oxen or sheep. This is what is called "richly drizzled." Being called "richly drizzled," what is it if not the first of the Eight Delicacies? When the aged are nourished with this, their vital energy and bodily frame are thereby strengthened.

When it is called "imitation rich" (chunmu), it is a dish made in imitation of "richly drizzled." When the former kings nourished the aged with the dish of "imitation rich," how then did they prepare it? Necessarily, they used fragrant broomcorn millet as its main ingredient. Frying meat to make a sauce and placing it atop the cooked millet is likewise by no means untasty; yet fearing it might not be fine enough, they would further blend it with the fat of chickens or dogs. This is what is called "imitation rich." Being called "imitation rich," what is it if not the second of the Eight Delicacies? When the aged are nourished with this, their blood and vital breath are thereby made flourishing.

Ah! In nourishing the aged, the ancients…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
之際而盡心如此非徒窮口腹之欲極飲食之精也
其亦示民以孝弟之教乎抑又論之八珍皆養老之
饌此特其二者爾下文各詳記之焉以是而觀可見
老者在所當尊而養之不可不備文王世子亦曰適
饌省醴養老之珍具即此意也是又不可不知
命酌曰請行觴酌者曰諾當飲者皆跪奉觴曰
賜灌勝者跪曰敬養
考試官教諭馮　批〔此作形容投壺之禮獻飲之際詞氣藹然〕
黄輔
===
其有得於恭儉莊敬之教者歟
考試官教諭鄭　批〔投壺一題非講之有素者不能發明至此〕
弟子承司射之命而行爵飲者受之以禮而不怨勝
者獻之以禮而不矜蓋投壺之禮有罰爵之行也司
射命勝黨弟子既舉而行之則受者不怨獻者不矜
其尊敬之意為何如哉記投壺者謂夫主人樂賓舉
行投壺之禮司射執筭以將主人之命及其卒也純
奇有辨優劣有別司射乃命勝黨之弟子酌酒以行
罰爵者焉弟子應之乃於西階上南面設豐洗觶升
punctuated:
之際，而盡心如此，非徒窮口腹之欲、極飲食之精也，其亦示民以孝弟之教乎！抑又論之，八珍皆養老之饌，此特其二者爾，下文各詳記之焉。以是而觀，可見老者在所當尊，而養之不可不備。《文王世子》亦曰：「適饌省醴，養老之珍具。」即此意也，是又不可不知。

「命酌曰：『請行觴。』酌者曰：『諾。』當飲者皆跪奉觴，曰：『賜灌。』勝者跪曰：『敬養。』」
考試官教諭馮　批〔此作形容投壺之禮、獻飲之際，詞氣藹然，其有得於恭儉莊敬之教者歟！〕
黄輔
考試官教諭鄭　批〔投壺一題，非講之有素者，不能發明至此。〕

弟子承司射之命而行爵，飲者受之以禮而不怨，勝者獻之以禮而不矜。蓋投壺之禮，有罰爵之行也。司射命勝黨弟子既舉而行之，則受者不怨，獻者不矜，其尊敬之意為何如哉！記《投壺》者謂夫主人樂賓，舉行投壺之禮，司射執筭以將主人之命。及其卒也，純奇有辨，優劣有別，司射乃命勝黨之弟子酌酒，以行罰爵者焉：『…』弟子應之，乃於西階上南面設豐，洗觶升…
translation_en:
…the aged, that they exerted their minds to such an extent—this was not merely to exhaust the desires of palate and belly or to carry the refinement of food and drink to the utmost; was it not also to show the people the teaching of filial piety and fraternal submission? Moreover, if we discuss it further, the Eight Delicacies are all viands for nourishing the aged, and these are merely two of them; the text below records each of them in detail. Viewed in this light, it can be seen that the aged are in a position that ought to be honored, and the nourishment provided for them must not be incomplete. The chapter "King Wen as Son and Heir" (Wen Wang shizi) also says: "He went to the viands and inspected the sweet wine, the precious provisions for nourishing the aged." This expresses the very same meaning, and it is something else that one must not fail to know.

"He commands the pourer, saying: 'Please pass the cup.' The pourer says: 'Yes.' Those who are to drink all kneel and hold up their cups, saying: 'You bestow a draught upon us.' The winners kneel and say: 'We respectfully nourish you.'"
Examiner and Confucian Instructor (jiaoyu) Feng comments: [This essay describes the rite of pitch-pot and the occasion of offering the drink with a warm and amiable tone; surely the writer has grasped the teaching of reverence, thrift,庄gravity, and respect found in the Classic of Rites!]
Huang Fu 黃輔
Examiner and Confucian Instructor (jiaoyu) Zheng comments: [On a topic like pitch-pot, no one who had not studied the text thoroughly beforehand could have elucidated it to this degree.]

The youths receive the command of the Director of Archery (sishe) to pass the cup; those who drink accept it according to ritual without resentment, and the winners offer it according to ritual without boasting. For in the rite of pitch-pot, there is the administration of the penalty cup. Once the Director of Archery commands the youths of the winning party to take it up and administer it, those who receive it bear no resentment and those who offer it show no boasting—how great is their spirit of respect and honor!

The writer who recorded the "Pitch-Pot" (Touhu) chapter meant to say that when the host entertains his guests and performs the rite of pitch-pot, the Director of Archery holds the tallies to carry out the host's commands. When the game is finished, pairs and odd tallies are distinguished, and superiority and inferiority are differentiated. The Director of Archery then commands the youths of the winning party to pour wine in order to administer the penalty cup, [saying: "Please pass the cup."] The youths answer in the affirmative, and thereupon set up the cup-stand facing south at the top of the western steps, wash the goblet, ascend…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
酌坐奠於豐之上斯時也當飲之人跪取豐上之酒
手捧之而致其辭曰賜灌謂蒙賜之飲也雖飲罰爵
能存服善之心而為尊敬之辭如此其受之以禮而
不怨也為何如勝者之人因彼飲者之敬亦跪之而
致其辭曰敬養言敬以此觴為奉養也雖行罰爵猶
為尊敬之辭以荅賜灌之辭如此其獻之以禮而不
矜也為何若噫投壺之禮乃射義之細故古人用之
以樂賓此其所以不廢也歟抑觀此一節飲其不勝
矣下文言正爵既行請立馬一馬從二馬以慶又以
飲其勝者焉繼之曰正爵既行請徹馬非掩其不勝
爾何衰其勝掩其不勝賓主之情藹然於阼階之間
尊敬之意歡歡於酬酢之頃夫投壺一用而禮義為備
也有如是哉
論
===
帝王一視同仁
同考試官訓導劉　批發揮一視同仁之旨洞然明白且筆勢滔
滔若河流東注一瀉千里讀之殊快人意誠傑作也
汪淶
punctuated:
酌，坐奠於豐之上。斯時也，當飲之人跪取豐上之酒，手捧之而致其辭曰：「賜灌。」謂蒙賜之飲也。雖飲罰爵，能存服善之心，而為尊敬之辭如此，其受之以禮而不怨也為何如！勝者之人，因彼飲者之敬，亦跪之而致其辭曰：「敬養。」言敬以此觴為奉養也。雖行罰爵，猶為尊敬之辭以荅「賜灌」之辭如此，其獻之以禮而不矜也為何若！噫，投壺之禮，乃射義之細，故古人用之以樂賓，此其所以不廢也歟！抑觀此一節，飲其不勝矣；下文言「正爵既行，請立馬，一馬從二馬以慶」，又以飲其勝者焉；繼之曰「正爵既行，請徹馬」，非掩其不勝爾何？衰其勝，掩其不勝，賓主之情藹然於阼階之間，尊敬之意歡歡於酬酢之頃。夫投壺一用，而禮義為備也有如是哉！

論
帝王一視同仁
汪淶
同考試官訓導劉　批：發揮「一視同仁」之旨，洞然明白，且筆勢滔滔，若河流東注，一瀉千里，讀之殊快人意，誠傑作也。
translation_en:
… pours the wine, and kneels to set the cup upon the stand (feng). At this moment, the person who is to drink kneels to take the wine from upon the stand, holds it in both hands, and offers the words: "You bestow a draught upon me" (ci guan)—meaning that he is favored with the gift of this drink. Even though he is drinking a penalty cup, he is able to preserve a heart that submits to excellence and utters such respectful words as these; how great is his receiving it with propriety and without resentment! Because of the drinker's respect, the winner also kneels to him and offers the words: "I respectfully offer nourishment" (jing yang)—meaning that he respectfully offers this goblet as sustenance. Even though he is administering a penalty cup, he still utters respectful words like these in reply to the words "You bestow a draught upon me"; how great is his presenting it with propriety and without boasting! Ah! The rite of pitch-pot (touhu) is a minor refinement of the meaning of archery, and so the ancients used it to delight their guests—is this not why it has never been abandoned? Moreover, looking at this passage, the loser is made to drink; the following text says, "When the regular cup has been drunk, permission is requested to set up the horse-tokens, and one horse is added to two horses in celebration," whereby the winner is also given to drink; and continuing, it says, "When the regular cup has been drunk, permission is requested to remove the horse-tokens"—what is this if not covering over the loser's defeat? By honouring [?] the victory and covering over the defeat, warm feelings between host and guest flourish harmoniously between the eastern and western steps, and sentiments of mutual respect are joyful in the moment of toasting and replying. That in a single performance of pitch-pot, ritual and righteousness are thus complete—how remarkable it is!

Discourse
"Emperors and Kings Regard All Equally with the Same Benevolence"
Wang Lai 汪淶
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Liu comments: It elucidates the purport of "regarding all equally with the same benevolence" with thorough clarity. Moreover, the momentum of the brush rolls on mightily, like a river rushing eastward for a thousand li in a single surge. Reading it is exceptionally gratifying to the mind—truly a masterpiece!

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭馮　批論有源委且識治體其形容而能發揮者歟
考試官教諭鄭　批發越本末略無餘蘊而議論帶出文勢雄
備非老學不能及此
論曰聖人之心何心哉仁天下之心也蓋天下
至大也風俗有剛柔之不同人品有賢愚之不
一而聖人仁天下之心果專於德化乎抑專於
威制乎以為專於德化也德但可以化賢而愚
者未能使之懷吾德是未之以語聖人仁天下
之心也以為專於威制也威但可以制愚而賢
===
者不可使之畏吾威亦未足以語聖人仁天下
之心也然則聖人仁天下之心果若之何耶不
專於德化不專於威制不泥於風俗不拘於人
品德以化之而威以制之仁以育之而政以養
之兼盡而無遺也並行而不悖也聖人仁天下
之心夫豈外於是哉愚嘗鑒諸天地矣時而春
夏也鼓之以雷霆潤之以風雨天地初何心哉
顯諸仁而已耳其所以顯之者固天地生生之
仁心時而秋冬也肅之以寒威慄之以霜雪天
punctuated:
考試官教諭馮　批：論有源委，且識治體，其形容而能發揮者歟！
考試官教諭鄭　批：發越本末，略無餘蘊，而議論帶出文勢雄備，非老學不能及此。

Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: It brings forth root and branch without leaving any meaning unexpressed, and the argument carries a vigorous and complete literary momentum. None but a seasoned scholar could attain this.

The discourse reads: What is the mind of the sage? It is a mind of benevolence toward all under Heaven. Now, all under Heaven is vast indeed: customs differ in being unyielding or pliant, and human characters vary in being worthy or foolish. Does the sage's mind of benevolence toward all under Heaven rely exclusively on transformation through virtue, or does it rely exclusively on restraint through awe-inspiring severity? If one takes it to rely exclusively on transformation through virtue, virtue can only transform the worthy, whereas the foolish cannot yet be made to cherish our virtue—this is insufficient [reading 未之以 as 未足以] to speak of the sage's mind of benevolence toward all under Heaven. If one takes it to rely exclusively on restraint through severity, severity can only restrain the foolish, whereas the worthy cannot be made to fear our severity—this too is insufficient to speak of the sage's mind of benevolence toward all under Heaven. If that is so, then what is the sage's mind of benevolence toward all under Heaven really like? It does not rely exclusively on transformation through virtue, nor does it rely exclusively on restraint through severity; it is not bogged down by customs, nor is it restricted by human characters. By virtue it transforms them and by severity it restrains them; by benevolence it nurtures them and by governance it sustains them. Both are fulfilled completely without omission, and both proceed together without contradiction. How could the sage's mind of benevolence toward all under Heaven be anything outside of this? title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:

天地生生之仁心然顯而弗藏則生者不能底
於成藏而非顯則成者不能以復生必一顯一
藏一生一成然後大以成大小以成小而天地
生生之仁始周流而無窮也聖人心天地之心
者也首出乎庶物之表卓冠乎群倫之先其治
天下也寧外於吾心之仁哉彼乃有人曰南方
風氣柔弱可以德化也殊不知君子可以德化
而南方之人未必皆君子亦未必不可以威制
===

風氣剛勁可以威制也殊不知小人可以威制
而北方之人未必皆小人亦未必不可以德化
也亦非善論聖人之治者矣善論聖人之治者

There must be alternating manifestation and concealment, alternating birth and completion; only then do the great become great and the small become small, and only then does the life-giving benevolence of Heaven and Earth circulate endlessly. The sage takes the mind of Heaven and Earth as his own mind. Rising preeminent above the multitude of things and standing supreme at the head of all human relationships, in governing the world, how could he depart from the benevolence of his own mind? They fail to realize that while a petty man can be restrained with severity, the people of the North are not necessarily all petty men, nor is it necessarily impossible to transform them through virtue. These people, too, are not good at discussing the governance of the sage. title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
道德為雨露漸之摩之甄之陶之使彼遵義遵
道者皆歸吾德化之中而一視同仁之心即天
地以生以育之心也制民也則以法制為霜雪
以禁令為寒威摧之折之慘之剝之使彼反道
敗德者悉歸吾大造之內而一視同仁之心即
天地以肅以殺之心也千萬其民則千萬其心
不必人人而化之化一人而千萬人化所以勸
千萬人也非一視之仁能如是乎億兆其民則
億兆其心不必人人而威之威一人而億兆人
===
畏所以懲億兆人也非一視之仁能若此乎善
者彰之惡者癉之一天地之陽舒而陰慘也君
子德之小人威之一天地之春生而秋殺也視
天下為一家而不泥於風俗之不同視中國猶
一人而不拘於人品之高下合德威而並施無
仁政而兩盡天下雖大也一心運之而有餘兆
民雖衆也一心化之而無間但見耕田而食鑿
井而飲相安於蕩蕩平平之域倫理以正恩義
以篤咸囿於不識不知之天斯時也天下一統
punctuated: 道德為雨露，漸之摩之，甄之陶之，使彼遵義遵道者皆歸吾德化之中，而一視同仁之心，即天地以生以育之心也。制民也，則以法制為霜雪，以禁令為寒威，摧之折之，慘之剝之，使彼反道敗德者悉歸吾大造之內，而一視同仁之心，即天地以肅以殺之心也。千萬其民則千萬其心，不必人人而化之，化一人而千萬人化，所以勸千萬人也，非一視之仁能如是乎？億兆其民則億兆其心，不必人人而威之，威一人而億兆人畏，所以懲億兆人也，非一視之仁能若此乎？善者彰之，惡者癉之，一天地之陽舒而陰慘也；君子德之，小人威之，一天地之春生而秋殺也。視天下為一家，而不泥於風俗之不同；視中國猶一人，而不拘於人品之高下。合德威而並施，無仁政而兩盡。天下雖大也，一心運之而有餘；兆民雖衆也，一心化之而無間。但見耕田而食，鑿井而飲，相安於蕩蕩平平之域；倫理以正，恩義以篤，咸囿於不識不知之天。斯時也，天下一統，
translation_en: … the Way and virtue as rain and dew, steeping them and polishing them, molding them and fashioning them, so that those who follow righteousness and follow the Way all come within the fold of our moral transformation; and this mind that regards all with equal benevolence is none other than Heaven and Earth's mind of giving life and nourishment. In restraining the people, he takes laws and institutions as frost and snow, and prohibitions and ordinances as cold and majesty, breaking them and bending them, afflicting them and stripping them, so that those who rebel against the Way and ruin virtue are all brought within our great creation; and this mind that regards all with equal benevolence is none other than Heaven and Earth's mind of severity and slaying. Where there are tens of millions of people, there are tens of millions of minds; one need not transform each person individually, for by transforming one person, tens of millions are transformed—this is how one encourages tens of millions. Could this be achieved without a benevolence that regards all equally? Where there are hundreds of millions of people, there are hundreds of millions of minds; one need not overawe each person individually, for by overawing one person, hundreds of millions are put in awe—this is how one warns hundreds of millions. Could this be so without a benevolence that regards all equally? Distinguishing the good and castigating the evil is entirely like the yang expansion and yin severity of Heaven and Earth; treating superior men with virtue and petty men with majesty is entirely like the spring life-giving and autumn slaying of Heaven and Earth. He regards all under Heaven as one family, without being bogged down by differences in customs; he regards the Central States as one person, without being bound by the high or low quality of human character. Combining virtue and majesty to apply them together, he embraces [?; 無] both benevolence and governance to the utmost. Though the empire is vast, he operates it with one mind and has capacity to spare; though the millions of people are multitude, he transforms them with one mind without any gap. title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
六合同春不寒威而民自畏也不霜雪而民自
服也威不必施矣刑不必加矣聖人於此夫何
為哉恭己乎南面之尊凝旒於九重之上無為
而天下治也垂拱而天下平也熙熙乎太古之
風皡皡乎淳厖之俗吾不知其孰為南孰為北
孰為君子孰為小人又不知孰可以德化孰可
以威制也論至於是則知聖人之心其天地之
心乎聖人之仁其天地之仁乎天地以生物為
心聖人以生民為心天地無棄物聖人無棄人
===
天地即聖人也聖人即天地也豈可以差殊觀
哉稽之於古唐虞之世堯推德以協和萬邦未
嘗德施於此而刑措於彼舜命官以明刑弼教
未嘗刑措於彼而德施於此當時黎民於變四
方風動非二帝一視同仁之明驗歟三代之時
大禹之祗台德先成湯之子惠困窮宜無恃於
威也而征伐之舉有不廢文王之惠鮮鰥寡武
王之重民五教宜無假於威也而一奮之怒有
不弛當時四海永清萬姓悅服非三王一視同
punctuated: 六合同春，不寒威而民自畏也，不霜雪而民自服也。威不必施矣，刑不必加矣。聖人於此，夫何為哉？恭己乎南面之尊，凝旒於九重之上，無為而天下治也，垂拱而天下平也。熙熙乎太古之風，皡皡乎淳厖之俗。吾不知其孰為南，孰為北，孰為君子，孰為小人，又不知孰可以德化，孰可以威制也。論至於是，則知聖人之心，其天地之心乎！聖人之仁，其天地之仁乎！天地以生物為心，聖人以生民為心；天地無棄物，聖人無棄人。天地即聖人也，聖人即天地也，豈可以差殊觀哉？稽之於古：唐虞之世，堯推德以協和萬邦，未嘗德施於此而刑措於彼；舜命官以明刑弼教，未嘗刑措於彼而德施於此。當時黎民於變，四方風動，非二帝一視同仁之明驗歟？三代之時，大禹之祗台德先，成湯之子惠困窮，宜無恃於威也，而征伐之舉有不廢；文王之惠鮮鰥寡，武王之重民五教，宜無假於威也，而一奮之怒有不弛。當時四海永清，萬姓悅服，非三王一視同
translation_en: …and the six directions share in the same spring. Without chill severity, the people naturally stand in awe; without frost and snow, the people naturally submit. Severity need no longer be applied, and punishments need no longer be imposed. At such a point, what does the sage need to do? He simply holds himself in reverent composure on the exalted throne facing south, his crown-tassels still high above in the ninefold palace; through non-action the world is governed, and by letting his robes hang down with hands folded, the world is brought to peace. How harmonious are the airs of high antiquity! How bright and contented are the pure and generous customs! I do not know who is of the south and who is of the north, who is a gentleman and who is a petty man; nor do I know who must be transformed by virtue and who must be restrained by awe. When the discussion reaches this point, one knows that the mind of the sage is indeed the mind of Heaven and Earth! The benevolence of the sage is indeed the benevolence of Heaven and Earth! Heaven and Earth take giving life to things as their mind, and the sage takes giving life to the people as his mind; Heaven and Earth abandon no thing, and the sage abandons no person. Heaven and Earth are none other than the sage, and the sage is none other than Heaven and Earth; how could they be viewed as different? At that time, the black-haired people were transformed and the four quarters were moved as by the wind—was this not clear proof of the two Emperors' impartial benevolence toward all alike? translation_en:
… clear proof that they regarded all with equal benevolence?

Reflecting deeply upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), he took the mind of Heaven and Earth as his mind, and practiced the benevolence of the emperors and kings as his benevolence. He used virtue to transform the people, and even when the people already cherished his virtue, in his mind he still considered them not yet transformed; he used majesty to restrain the people, and even when the people already stood in awe of his majesty, in his mind he still considered them not yet submitted. Thus, in the leisure from his myriad affairs of state, he discussed and debated the Way of governance with his attending officials, saying: "Though the land has south and north, the people do not have two minds; an emperor or king regards all with equal benevolence—how could there be any distinction between this and that?" Great indeed are the August Words! Unified indeed is the August Mind! Is this not whereby he established a mind for Heaven and Earth, established a destiny for the living people, and opened up great peace for ten thousand generations? Ah! The mind with which the Grand Progenitor treated all under Heaven with benevolence is supremely great and difficult to name. As for one capable of continuing the glorious achievements of the past, whose mind is one with Heaven and Earth and whose virtue crowns that of the emperors and kings, today we are fortunate to have the Sacred Son of Heaven reigning above.

Moreover, the cycle of destiny truly matches an era of great peace, and the military strategy accords perfectly with the workings of Heaven. Court and countryside rejoice together; ministers and aides all celebrate.

Respectfully reflecting upon [Your Majesty, the Emperor], who is perceptive, wise, and sagacious, civil, martial, sacred, and divine: You have inherited the grand foundation of the successive sacred emperors and received the favored mandate of High Heaven. Vigorously sweeping away long-standing abuses, You shine the brilliance of the Li trigram across the four quarters; skillfully employing loyal counsel, You hold fast to the firmness of the Qian trigram and decide alone. With pendant-strands composed, You stand in the space between the throne and the screen, counting tribute and examining the maps of the realm.

Yet look upon that petty region of Huai and Cai, which dared to indulge in the wickedness of blocking imperial orders [?]. Illegitimately passed down through three surnames, they relied on the sharpness and obstinacy of their soldiers; as our past campaigns dragged on for four years, one lamented the blunting and loss of our military prestige. When plans were made to renew the punitive expedition, all said they should be won over by grace [?]. Though the multitude of opinions was confused and reached no consensus, Heaven's punishment had to be inflicted without any shrinking back.

Our general roused a might like that of leopards and tigers, and thus deployed our army; maintaining an awe both solemn and disciplined, our renown reached the four seas and our majesty shook the eight wildernesses. Gagging the soldiers and beating drums, we startled the geese and swans to mask the sound of the army [?]; cutting off the left ears of the slain and seizing captives, our forces marched through the night snow with surging martial ferocity. I have heard it said that wherever there is the ruler of an era, there are the canonical institutions of that era. Prior to us, for the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, the facts of their deeds were recorded in the Classics; later, for the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song, the facts of their deeds were chronicled in the Histories. In what is recorded in the Classics, there are assuredly no flaws that can be criticized; in what is chronicled in the Histories, however, there are successes and failures that can be discussed. Yet that which surpasses Han, Tang, and Song and can rival the splendor of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—is it not solely the institutions of our Dynasty? Profound indeed is the necessity of examining the Veritable Records (Shilu)! Allow me to verify this against antiquity and measure it against the present in order to reply to the brilliant question.

Ever since antiquity, those who ruled as emperors in Tang and Yu were Yao and Shun; those who ruled as kings in Xia, Shang, and Zhou were Yu and Tang, Wen and Wu. title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
闕庭都俞吁咈之辨容危微精一之授受齊天
運有羲和之曆定地理有禹貢之書務學則說
命爲入道之門論治則洪範爲經世之要他如
周官之訓迪無逸之教戒大經大法胥此焉出
嘉謨嘉猷於是乎存此帝王行實之載於經者
豈容議於其間哉迨至漢人䌷蘭臺之秘藏發
金匱之舊籍鋪張一代之美而有實錄之名其
書曰本紀曰世家曰書曰表書非不詳矣然帝
紀列呂氏不能無譏於房闥之政八書著封禪
===
不能無憾於登封之舉漢之實錄果足於漢之
治乎唐沿漢制高祖之實錄二十卷而太宗則
六十卷焉憲宗之實錄四十卷而德宗則五十
卷焉書非不備矣然敬宗之曲筆未免有失實
之嫌韓愈之直書又起後來竄定之議唐之實
錄果直紀唐之事乎降及於宋搜尋有詔訪求
有命而實錄之書益備矣提舉以宰臣脩撰以
侍從而實錄之官益重矣或專置院或寓史館
而實錄之地益崇矣若太祖實錄凡五十卷李
punctuated: 闕庭都俞吁咈之辨容，危微精一之授受，齊天運有羲和之曆，定地理有《禹貢》之書，務學則《說命》爲入道之門，論治則《洪範》爲經世之要。他如《周官》之訓迪、《無逸》之教戒，大經大法胥此焉出，嘉謨嘉猷於是乎存。此帝王行實之載於經者，豈容議於其間哉？迨至漢人，䌷蘭臺之秘藏，發金匱之舊籍，鋪張一代之美，而有「實錄」之名。其書曰本紀、曰世家、曰書、曰表，書非不詳矣；然帝紀列呂氏，不能無譏於房闥之政，八書著封禪，不能無憾於登封之舉。漢之實錄，果足於漢之治乎？唐沿漢制，《高祖之實錄》二十卷，而《太宗》則六十卷焉；《憲宗之實錄》四十卷，而《德宗》則五十卷焉。書非不備矣；然敬宗之曲筆，未免有失實之嫌，韓愈之直書，又起後來竄定之議。唐之實錄，果直紀唐之事乎？降及於宋，搜尋有詔，訪求有命，而實錄之書益備矣；提舉以宰臣，脩撰以侍從，而實錄之官益重矣；或專置院，或寓史館，而實錄之地益崇矣。若《太祖實錄》凡五十卷，李
translation_en: … the discerning demeanor in the exclamations of agreement and disagreement at the palace court; the transmission and reception of the teaching on the precariousness of the human mind, the subtlety of the moral mind, and remaining discerning and undivided; for regulating the movements of Heaven, there was the calendar of Xi and He; for determining the configuration of the earth, there was the document Tribute of Yu (Yu gong); for devoting oneself to learning, the Charge to Yue (Yue ming) served as the gateway to entering the Way; for discussing governance, the Great Plan (Hong fan) served as the essential guide for ordering the world. As for others, such as the instructions and guidance of the Officers of Zhou (Zhou guan) and the teachings and admonitions of Against Luxurious Ease (Wu yi)—great principles and great laws all emerged from these, and admirable counsels and admirable plans were preserved herein. These are the actual deeds of emperors and kings recorded in the Classics; how could any criticism be permitted among them? Coming down to the men of Han, they drew out the secret treasures of the Orchid Terrace and opened the old records of the golden coffers, magnifying the splendors of an entire era, and thus came to have the name "Veritable Records" (shilu). Their work was divided into Basic Annals (benji), Hereditary Houses (shijia), Treatises (shu), and Tables (biao). The writing was certainly not lacking in detail; yet the Imperial Annals included Empress Lü, which cannot escape criticism regarding governance from the inner quarters, and the Eight Treatises recorded the Feng and Shan sacrifices, which cannot escape regret over the act of ascending Mount Tai to perform the Feng sacrifice. Were the Veritable Records of Han truly adequate to the governance of Han? The Tang followed the Han institution: the Veritable Records of Gaozu (Gaozu zhi shilu) comprised twenty scrolls, while those of Taizong comprised sixty scrolls; the Veritable Records of Xianzong (Xianzong zhi shilu) comprised forty scrolls, while those of Dezong comprised fifty scrolls. The writings were certainly not incomplete; yet the distorted brush of Xu Jingzong could not avoid the suspicion of departing from the truth, and the straightforward writing of Han Yu in turn gave rise to subsequent controversies over tampering and revision. Did the Veritable Records of Tang truly record the affairs of Tang straightforwardly? Coming down to the Song, there were edicts to search out materials and commands to make inquiries, so the books of the Veritable Records became ever more complete; Grand Councilors served as Directors (tiju) and court attendants served as Compilers (xiuzhuan), so the officials of the Veritable Records became ever more weighty; either a dedicated institute was established or it was housed in the Historiography Institute, so the place of the Veritable Records became ever more exalted. For instance, the Veritable Records of Taizu (Taizu shilu), totaling fifty scrolls, was compiled by Li…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
昉葺之所纂也太宗實錄凡八十卷錢若水之
所脩也然哲宗元祐之治多汚於京卞之手徽
宗崇觀之事亦出於蔡京之姦豈盡實錄之真
哉此漢唐宋之制作或業鉅而辭淺或文浮而
實濊其得失不能無可言者矣洪惟
天朝
聖聖相承豐功茂德蕩蕩乎天地之大英聲美號昭
昭乎日月之明我
太祖高皇帝萬幾之暇御製大誥三編必親為之撫
拾而其勸善懲惡之實為可見
===
太宗文皇帝庶務之餘御製為善陰隲孝順事實二
書必親為之詩斷而其勸善行孝之實又可見
宣宗章皇帝推廣
列聖之明訓采輯群書之所載類集為五倫書則所
以明人倫而美風化之實又可見矣
英宗睿皇帝丕纘鴻休益隆治道
神功聖德冊植于宇宙宏規懿範久愜于人心嗚
呼盛矣方今
punctuated: 昉葺之所纂也；《太宗實錄》凡八十卷，錢若水之所脩也。然哲宗元祐之治，多汚於京、卞之手；徽宗崇、觀之事，亦出於蔡京之姦，豈盡《實錄》之真哉？此漢、唐、宋之制作，或業鉅而辭淺，或文浮而實濊，其得失不能無可言者矣。洪惟天朝，聖聖相承，豐功茂德，蕩蕩乎天地之大；英聲美號，昭昭乎日月之明。我太祖高皇帝萬幾之暇，御製《大誥》三編，必親為之撫拾，而其勸善懲惡之實為可見；太宗文皇帝庶務之餘，御製《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，必親為之詩斷，而其勸善行孝之實又可見；宣宗章皇帝推廣列聖之明訓，采輯群書之所載，類集為《五倫書》，則所以明人倫而美風化之實又可見矣。英宗睿皇帝丕纘鴻休，益隆治道，神功聖德，冊植于宇宙；宏規懿範，久愜于人心。嗚呼盛矣！方今
translation_en:
… compiled by Li Fang 李昉 and others [葺 for 輩?]; the Veritable Records of Taizong (Taizong shilu) in eighty juan in all was compiled by Qian Ruoshui 錢若水. Yet the governance of the Yuanyou reign of Emperor Zhezong was largely defiled at the hands of Cai Jing 蔡京 and Cai Bian 蔡卞, and the affairs of the Chongning and Daguan reigns of Emperor Huizong likewise issued from the treachery of Cai Jing—how could these fully represent the truth of Veritable Records? In such literary productions of the Han, Tang, and Song, either the achievements were vast while the words were shallow, or the writing was华麗 [superficial] while the substance was sullied [濊 for 穢?]; one cannot but have something to say about their merits and defects.

Reflecting upon our Heavenly Dynasty, sage has succeeded sage; their abundant merits and flourishing virtue are as vast and boundless as Heaven and Earth, and their heroic renown and fine titles are as bright and resplendent as the sun and moon. Our Emperor Taizu Gaohuangdi, in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, imperially composed the Three Compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao sanbian), personally gathering the material for them, so that the substance of his encouraging goodness and punishing evil can be seen. Emperor Taizong Wenhuangdi, in his spare time from general administrative duties, imperially composed the two books Rewards for Doing Good Secretly Determined by Heaven (Weishan yinzhi) and True Examples of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi), personally writing poetic judgments for each entry, so that the substance of his encouraging goodness and practicing filial piety can again be seen. Emperor Xuanzong Zhanghuangdi extended the luminous instructions of the successive sages, selected and compiled accounts recorded in various books, and categorized and collected them into the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), whereby the substance of his clarifying human relationships and beautifying customs and moral transformation can again be seen. Emperor Yingzong Ruihuangdi grandly continued the great blessings and further exalted the way of governance; his divine achievements and sagely virtue were implanted [冊植 for 蟠植?] throughout the universe, and his vast plans and admirable models have long satisfied the hearts of the people. Oh, how glorious! At present, …

text:
皇上嗣承大統首命文臣纂脩實錄其所以仰紹
前烈而啓裕後世之意至矣誠萬世不刊之大典也
由是而知
列聖之制作雖先後不同而同一精神心術之所寓

其與書之虞廷賡歌同一歸申明五常之條其

作不善降之百殃即陰隲之勸善也書載虞舜
克諧之孝君陳孝恭之德即孝實之行孝也五
===
倫書之編輯與今實錄之纂脩又何異於書之
所載乎此
列聖之心一堯舜禹湯文武之心
列聖之書一典謨訓誥誓命之書是即孟子所謂先
聖後聖其揆一也愚也身際
隆平之時目覩
制作之盛謹拜手稽首而對揚
王休於萬一焉
第二問
punctuated:
皇上嗣承大統，首命文臣纂脩《實錄》，其所以仰紹前烈而啓裕後世之意至矣，誠萬世不刊之大典也。由是而知列聖之制作，雖先後不同，而同一精神心術之所寓也，同一仁義道德之所發也。若君臣同遊之語，其與《書》之虞廷賡歌同一歸；申明五常之條，其與《書》之敬敷五教同一致。《書》謂「作善，降之百祥；作不善，降之百殃」，即《陰隲》之勸善也；《書》載虞舜克諧之孝、君陳孝恭之德，即《孝實》之行孝也。《五倫書》之編輯，與今《實錄》之纂脩，又何異於《書》之所載乎？此列聖之心，一堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心；列聖之書，一典、謨、訓、誥、誓、命之書。是即孟子所謂「先聖後聖，其揆一也」。愚也身際隆平之時，目覩制作之盛，謹拜手稽首，而對揚王休於萬一焉。
第二問
translation_en:
…His Majesty succeeded to the Great Succession and as his first act commanded his civil officials to compile the Veritable Records (Shilu). In this, his intention of reverently continuing the achievements of his predecessors and enlightening and enriching posterity reaches the utmost perfection; truly, it is a great canon immutable for ten thousand generations! From this we may know that although the creations of the Successive Sages were produced at different times, they are the abode of the very same spirit and mental art, and the manifestation of the very same benevolence, righteousness, morality, and virtue. For instance, the words of A Record of Sovereign and Ministers Touring Together (Junchen tongyou) share the same ultimate aim as the antiphonal songs of the court of Yu in the Book of Documents (Shu); the articles reiterating and clarifying the Five Constant Virtues reach the same end as the reverent dissemination of the Five Teachings in the Book of Documents. When the Book of Documents says, "On him who does good, He sends down all blessings; on him who does not do good, He sends down all calamities," this is none other than the exhortation to goodness in Silent Recompense for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi); when the Book of Documents records the filial piety of Shun of Yu in achieving harmony and the filial and reverent virtue of Junchen, this is none other than the practice of filial piety in True Examples of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi). And how do the compilation of the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) and the present compilation of the Veritable Records differ from what is recorded in the Book of Documents? Thus, the mind of the Successive Sages is identical with the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu; the books of the Successive Sages are identical with the books of the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, Announcements, Oaths, and Charges. This is precisely what Mencius meant when he said, "The former sages and the latter sages—their principles are one." Ignorant as I am, personally encountering an era of flourishing peace and witnessing with my own eyes the splendor of these imperial creations, I respectfully bow my hands and knock my head to the ground to extol in reply even one ten-thousandth part of the royal beneficence.

矣試以西蜀觀之山川蔥欝氣象宏富其鍾於
===
物也則為青金丹砂之良其鍾於人也則為先
明俊傑之美故以漢唐宋言之司馬長卿黃門
奏賦飄飄凌雲似也然臨邛失節而終身有慚
焉揚子雲白首草玄甘心辭莫固也然劇秦美
新而名教有玷焉若甘心肥遯不事王侯忠孝
一言有裨風教此嚴君平也較彼二人則其優
劣可見矣作頌漢庭諂諛君臣王襃善文辭也
而彭祖喬松之語識者陋之賦詩沉香奕奕風
月李白善詩章也而失身叢逆之嫌君子惜之
punctuated:
李文中
考試官教諭馮批：〔條答古人事實，明白簡要，而篇終一段見佳，可見學識之正。〕
考試官教諭鄭批：〔考事核，斷制明，策場中之表表者。〕
品第乎人物者，固當以德行為先；景行乎前哲者，尤當以德行為法。蓋德行，本也；而文章，乃其餘事耳。則夫品第人物而景仰前哲者，烏可不知所當先與所當法者乎？知此，則可以復明問矣。試以西蜀觀之，山川蔥欝，氣象宏富，其鍾於物也，則為青金、丹砂之良；其鍾於人也，則為先明、俊傑之美。故以漢、唐、宋言之：司馬長卿黃門奏賦，飄飄凌雲，似也；然臨邛失節，而終身有慚焉。揚子雲白首草《玄》，甘心辭莫，固也；然劇秦美新，而名教有玷焉。若甘心肥遯，不事王侯，忠孝一言，有裨風教，此嚴君平也。較彼二人，則其優劣可見矣。作頌漢庭，諂諛君臣，王襃善文辭也；而彭祖、喬、松之語，識者陋之。賦詩沉香，奕奕風月，李白善詩章也；而失身叢逆之嫌，君子惜之。
translation_en:
Li Wenzhong
Examiner and Instructor Feng comments: [He answers item by item regarding the historical facts of the ancients clearly and concisely, and the final section of the piece shows fine insight, demonstrating the correctness of his scholarship and understanding.]
Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: [His verification of facts is accurate and his judgments are clear; it is an outstanding piece in the policy examination session.]
Those who evaluate and rank historical figures should certainly put moral conduct first; those who look up to and emulate former sages should especially take moral conduct as their model. For moral conduct is the root, whereas literary composition is merely a secondary matter. How, then, could anyone who ranks historical figures and admires former sages fail to know what ought to be put first and what ought to be taken as a model? Knowing this, one can reply to the enlightened question. Let us examine Western Shu (Sichuan): its mountains and rivers are lush and verdant, its aspect grand and abundant. When its vital energy is concentrated in things, it becomes the excellence of blue-gold lead and cinnabar; when concentrated in people, it becomes the beauty of enlightened [?] and outstanding heroes. Therefore, to speak of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties: Sima Changqing (Sima Xiangru 司馬相如) presented rhapsodies at the Yellow Gates, soaring high above the clouds—so it seems; yet he lost his integrity at Linqiong, bearing shame for the rest of his life. Yang Ziyun (Yang Xiong 揚雄) drafted the Classic of Great Mystery (Taixuan) with a white head, content in quietude [?], to be sure; yet in criticizing the Qin and praising the Xin dynasty, he left a blemish upon Confucian moral teachings. As for one who was content to live in comfortable reclusion, refusing to serve kings and marquises, whose single word on loyalty and filial piety aided moral instruction—this was Yan Junping (嚴君平). Comparing him with those two men, their relative superiority and inferiority can be seen. Composing eulogies in the Han court and flattering ruler and ministers, Wang Bao (王襃) excelled in literary rhetoric; yet discerning men despised his talk of Pengzu, Wangzi Qiao, and Chisongzi. Composing poems at the Aloeswood Pavilion, radiant as the wind and moon, Li Bai (李白) excelled in poetic verse; yet gentlemen lamented the suspicion of his having compromised himself among rebels.…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
若秉心立朝有意規諫奏論數章皆切大體非
陳子昂乎較彼二人則其優劣可知矣此西蜀
人物之在漢唐者果在於文章而不在於德行
歟五季既衰有宋混一日藁月滋教化相漸偉
人碩德後先相望仁宗之無嗣難言也而范景
仁首議之孰可及其勇決乎王安石之姦未形
也而蘇老泉能辨之孰可及其先見乎稱東坡
曰天下奇才而不知僭耳之遊其氣可以狙金
石而凌雪霜稱穎濵曰制策翩翩而不知□法
===
之跡其言可以質天地而感鬼神范鴻夫之經
學非學也色和氣柔開悟上意其學粹矣留公
錫之奏議非文也憂治世而危明主其文雅矣
孝以事親甘露降祥彭公乘之孝而人曰今之
曾參也廉以律己上悟帝意孫公抃之廉而人
曰今之伯夷也此西蜀人物之在有宋者則在
於德行而不在於文章矣雖然攻於文者或技
葉之是求若所謂孝乃其德行而不可以論焉
也強於學者或口耳之是習若所謂廉乃其甘
punctuated: 若秉心立朝，有意規諫，奏論數章，皆切大體，非陳子昂乎？較彼二人，則其優劣可知矣。此西蜀人物之在漢、唐者，果在於文章而不在於德行歟？五季既衰，有宋混一，日藁月滋，教化相漸，偉人碩德，後先相望。仁宗之無嗣難言也，而范景仁首議之，孰可及其勇決乎？王安石之姦未形也，而蘇老泉能辨之，孰可及其先見乎？稱東坡曰「天下奇才」，而不知僭耳之遊，其氣可以狙金石而凌雪霜；稱穎濵曰「制策翩翩」，而不知□法之跡，其言可以質天地而感鬼神。范鴻夫之經學非學也，色和氣柔，開悟上意，其學粹矣；留公錫之奏議非文也，憂治世而危明主，其文雅矣。孝以事親，甘露降祥，彭公乘之孝，而人曰「今之曾參」也；廉以律己，上悟帝意，孫公抃之廉，而人曰「今之伯夷」也。此西蜀人物之在有宋者，則在於德行而不在於文章矣。雖然，攻於文者或技葉之是求，若所謂孝，乃其德行而不可以論焉也；強於學者或口耳之是習，若所謂廉，乃其甘
translation_en:
As for one who upheld a sincere heart at court and was intent on remonstrance, submitting several memorials and discourses that all struck at fundamental principles—was this not Chen Zi'ang 陳子昂? Comparing him with those two men [Wang Bao and Li Bai], their relative merits can be known. Thus, as for the notable figures of Western Shu in the Han and Tang dynasties, did their worth truly lie in literary composition and not in moral conduct?

Once the Five Dynasties declined and the Song unified the realm, with daily cultivation [?] and monthly growth, moral transformation gradually soaked in, and great men of eminent virtue appeared one after another. That Emperor Renzong 仁宗 lacked an heir was a difficult matter to speak of, yet Fan Jingren 范景仁 (Fan Zhen 范鎮) was the first to raise it for discussion—who could match his courageous resolve? When the treachery of Wang Anshi 王安石 had not yet taken form, Su Laoquan 蘇老泉 (Su Xun 蘇洵) was able to discern it—who could match his foresight? People praised Dongpo 東坡 (Su Shi 蘇軾) as an "extraordinary talent of the empire," yet failed to recognize that in his journey to Danzhou [? 僭耳 for 儋耳], his spirit could pierce [?] metal and stone and brave snow and frost. People praised Yingbin 穎濵 (Su Zhe 蘇轍) for his "graceful palace examination essays," yet failed to recognize that in his critiques of the New Policies [? □法之跡], his words could stand before Heaven and Earth and move ghosts and spirits.

The classical scholarship of Fan Hongfu 范鴻夫 [? for Fan Chunfu 范淳夫 (Fan Zuyu 范祖禹)] was not mere book-learning: with a gentle countenance and mild demeanor, he enlightened the Emperor's mind—his scholarship was pure indeed! The memorials of Lord Liu Xi 留公錫 [? for Tian Xi 田錫] were not mere literary prose: worrying in an age of order and warning an enlightened ruler of peril, his writing was principled indeed! Serving his parents with filial piety so that sweet dew descended as an auspicious omen—such was the filial piety of Lord Peng Cheng 彭公乘, of whom people said, "He is a Zeng Shen 曾參 of the present day." Regulating himself with integrity so as to awaken the Emperor's understanding above—such was the integrity of Lord Sun Bian 孫公抃, of whom people said, "He is a Boyi 伯夷 of the present day." Thus, as for the notable figures of Western Shu in the Song dynasty, their worth lay in moral conduct and not merely in literary composition.

Even so, those who specialize in literature perhaps seek only twigs and leaves [? 技葉 for 枝葉]; as for what is called filial piety, that is a matter of moral conduct and cannot be fabricated [? 論焉]. Those who strive in learning perhaps practice only what enters the ear and leaves the mouth; as for what is called integrity, that is their [actual? 甘 for 實] …

行而不可以矯飾也愚也生長西蜀景行先哲
有文章者非在所輕而有德行者實在所重故
求之孝似可法也其果曾參之養志乎朽之廉
若可法也其果伯夷聖之清乎嘗觀孔子之教
人矣一則以德行爲首科而文學爲之後二則
以德行爲先務而文藝爲之末必如是焉庶幾
乎其無弊矣孟子曰乃所願則學孔子也請以
是爲終篇獻
第三問
陳鳳

其效蓋爲治固在於教養而法亦不可不任也
古人爲治各務其實而今人徒徇其名此所以
有常享乎祀與未臻其效者歟請條陳之西蜀
punctuated:
行，而不可以矯飾也。愚也生長西蜀，景行先哲。有文章者，非在所輕；而有德行者，實在所重。故求之孝似可法也，其果曾參之養志乎？朽之廉若可法也，其果伯夷聖之清乎？嘗觀孔子之教人矣：一則以德行爲首科，而文學爲之後；二則以德行爲先務，而文藝爲之末。必如是焉，庶幾乎其無弊矣。孟子曰：「乃所願，則學孔子也。」請以是爲終篇獻。

第三問
陳鳳
同考試官教授劉　批〔酌古準今，處置當理，使見諸用，必有可觀。〕

爲治務實者，有以享其祀；爲治徇名者，無以臻其效。蓋爲治固在於教養，而法亦不可不任也。古人爲治，各務其實；而今人徒徇其名。此所以有常享乎祀，與未臻其效者歟！請條陳之。西蜀
translation_en:
… conduct, and cannot be feigned or embellished. I, in my ignorance, was born and raised in Western Shu, and I look up to the worthy exemplars of the past. Those who possess literary skill are not to be slighted, yet those who possess moral conduct are truly what must be valued. Thus, if Peng Cheng's [transcribed 求, ?] filial piety seems worthy of emulation, did it truly match Zeng Shen's nourishing of his parents' will? If Sun Bian's [transcribed 朽, ?] integrity seems worthy of emulation, did it truly match Bo Yi's sagely purity? I have observed how Confucius taught others: first, he made moral conduct the foremost category and placed literature and learning after it; second, he made moral conduct the primary task and treated the polite arts as secondary. Only when it is done like this can it perhaps be free of faults. Mencius said: "What I wish to do is to learn from Confucius." I beg to offer this as the conclusion to my essay.

text:
之地古諸州之域號天府之國物之産也瑰奇
人之生也俊秀夫何難治爲哉觀夫秦李冰之
爲守也因水患之未除則作石人以止江水作
石犀以壓水精鑿離堆山分派灌溉欲民之足
其衣也則勸之以治桑欲民之足其食也則勸
之以治田此養民之務其實也爲何如漢文翁
之爲守也因民性之未復則起脩學舍選擇儒
官遣小吏於京師皆卒業而歸招子弟於郡縣
悉聞風而至文教之振彷彿乎鄒魯之風倫理
===
之正一洗乎蠻夷之習此教民之務其實也又
何如迨宋咸平淳化間而張詠兩治乎蜀剛方
自任威惠並施嚴厲明斷以制姦暴公平信義
以善風俗屢按一發而百姓驚嘆號令一下而
群情慰愜又非張詠治民之實務乎之三公者
或教養或任法而各臻其實效所謂有功德於
民者也是宜設廟貌以事之備祀禮以享之綿
綿乎迄于今而不窮焉前代之守蜀者如此然
則我
punctuated: 之地，古諸州之域，號天府之國。物之産也瑰奇，人之生也俊秀，夫何難治爲哉？觀夫秦李冰之爲守也，因水患之未除，則作石人以止江水，作石犀以壓水精，鑿離堆山，分派灌溉。欲民之足其衣也，則勸之以治桑；欲民之足其食也，則勸之以治田。此養民之務其實也爲何如！漢文翁之爲守也，因民性之未復，則起脩學舍，選擇儒官；遣小吏於京師，皆卒業而歸；招子弟於郡縣，悉聞風而至。文教之振，彷彿乎鄒魯之風；倫理之正，一洗乎蠻夷之習。此教民之務其實也又何如！迨宋咸平、淳化間，而張詠兩治乎蜀，剛方自任，威惠並施，嚴厲明斷以制姦暴，公平信義以善風俗。屢按一發而百姓驚嘆，號令一下而群情慰愜，又非張詠治民之實務乎？之三公者，或教養，或任法，而各臻其實效，所謂有功德於民者也。是宜設廟貌以事之，備祀禮以享之，綿綿乎迄于今而不窮焉。前代之守蜀者如此，然則我
translation_en: …of Western Shu is the territory of the ancient provinces, renowned as a "Land of Abundance." Its material products are wondrous and rare, and the people born here are talented and refined—why then should it be difficult to govern? Observe how, when Li Bing 李冰 of the Qin served as its Governor (太守), because the calamity of floods had not yet been eliminated, he erected stone human figures to check the river's waters, made stone rhinoceroses to suppress the water sprites, and cut through Mount Lidui 離堆山 to divide the currents for irrigation. Wishing the people to have sufficient clothing, he encouraged them to cultivate mulberry trees; wishing the people to have sufficient food, he encouraged them to cultivate their fields. What a splendid example of attending to the reality of nourishing the people this was! When Wen Weng 文翁 of the Han served as its Governor, because the nature of the people had not yet been restored to goodness, he built and repaired schoolhouses and selected Confucian instructors; he sent minor subofficial functionaries to the capital, who all completed their studies and returned; and he recruited young men from the commanderies and counties, who all heard of this cultural wind and came. The flourishing of cultural education closely resembled the customs of Zou 鄒 and Lu 魯, and the rectification of human moral relations completely washed away the habits of the southern and eastern barbarians. What a splendid example of attending to the reality of educating the people this too was! Coming down to the Xianping 咸平 (998–1003) and Chunhua 淳化 (990–994) eras of the Song, Zhang Yong 張詠 twice governed Shu. Taking firm uprightness as his personal responsibility and applying both awe-inspiring authority and benevolence, he used sternness and clear decisiveness to restrain the wicked and violent, and fairness, impartiality, trustworthiness, and righteousness to improve popular customs. When he repeatedly investigated cases and exposed them at a stroke, the common people marveled in admiration; as soon as his orders were issued, popular sentiment was comforted and satisfied. Was this not in turn Zhang Yong's practical work in governing the people? These three worthies either educated and nourished the people or relied upon the law, yet each achieved real results; they are what is meant by those who have rendered meritorious service and virtuous benefit to the people. Thus it is fitting that shrines and images have been established to serve them, and sacrificial rites prepared to make offerings to them, continuing unbroken down to the present day without end. Those who governed Shu in former dynasties were like this; how then do those of our…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
朝之守蜀者何如其間有開塘深陂穿渠引水溝
洫充滿而水利益增宜其有家給人足之效矣
而其效未能多見者蓋以守此地者特徇治水
之名而無勸農之實故耳為今之計誠能體
朝廷養民之心如李冰之治水利勸民農桑而實
用其力尚何患衣食之不足哉鄉閭有學郡邑
有庠訓迪髦髦而學政益脩宜其有反薄歸厚
之俗矣而其俗未盡丕變者蓋以守此土者特
徇教學之名而無躬行之實故耳為今之計誠
===
能體
朝廷教民之意如文翁之興學校教民復性而實
盡其心尚何慮風俗之不美哉一蜀之民有善
有惡彼強惡者繩之以法宜矣苟徒有繩惡之
名而所施未盡宜焉則惡者且不知懼而欲其
惡之加少得乎彼柔善者撫之以恩當矣苟徒
有撫善之名而所施未盡當焉則善者且不知
勸而欲其善之加多又可得乎故必公於繩惡
若張詠之嚴厲明斷則將威一人而千萬人服
punctuated: 朝之守蜀者何如？其間有開塘深陂、穿渠引水，溝洫充滿而水利益增，宜其有家給人足之效矣。而其效未能多見者，蓋以守此地者特徇治水之名，而無勸農之實故耳。為今之計，誠能體朝廷養民之心，如李冰之治水利，勸民農桑而實用其力，尚何患衣食之不足哉？鄉閭有學，郡邑有庠，訓迪髦髦而學政益脩，宜其有反薄歸厚之俗矣。而其俗未盡丕變者，蓋以守此土者特徇教學之名，而無躬行之實故耳。為今之計，誠能體朝廷教民之意，如文翁之興學校，教民復性而實盡其心，尚何慮風俗之不美哉？一蜀之民有善有惡，彼強惡者繩之以法，宜矣；苟徒有繩惡之名，而所施未盡宜焉，則惡者且不知懼，而欲其惡之加少，得乎？彼柔善者撫之以恩，當矣；苟徒有撫善之名，而所施未盡當焉，則善者且不知勸，而欲其善之加多，又可得乎？故必公於繩惡，若張詠之嚴厲明斷，則將威一人而千萬人服，
translation_en:
… dynasty's officials governing Shu—how have they fared? Among them there have been those who dug ponds, deepened reservoirs, cut canals, and channeled water, so that irrigation ditches were filled to the brim and water conservancy benefits steadily increased; one would expect this to have had the effect of making every household well-provided and every person self-sufficient. Yet the reason such effects have rarely been seen is simply that those who govern this region merely pursue the reputation of managing water without the reality of encouraging agriculture. As a plan for today, if they can truly embody the Imperial Court's heart for nourishing the people—regulating water conservancy as Li Bing 李冰 did, encouraging the people in farming and sericulture, and genuinely exerting their efforts—then what worry would there still be of an insufficiency of food and clothing?

Villages and neighborhoods have their schools, and prefectures and counties have their academies, instructing and guiding the promising youth [?] (髦髦) so that educational administration is increasingly cultivated; one would expect this to have brought about customs that turn away from frivolity and return to generosity. Yet the reason the customs have not been completely and greatly transformed is simply that those who govern this land merely pursue the reputation of teaching and learning without the reality of personal practice. As a plan for today, if they can truly embody the Imperial Court's intention of educating the people—establishing schools as Wen Weng 文翁 did, teaching the people to recover their moral nature, and genuinely exhausting their hearts in doing so—then what anxiety would there still be that customs might not be admirable?

Among the people of all Shu, there are the good and the wicked. As for the fiercely wicked, it is right to restrain them with the law; yet if one merely has the reputation of restraining the wicked while the measures applied are not entirely fitting, then the wicked will not even know fear—and is it possible then to hope that their wickedness will decrease? As for the gentle and good, it is proper to comfort them with grace; yet if one merely has the reputation of comforting the good while the measures applied are not entirely proper, then the good will not even know encouragement—and is it possible then to hope that their goodness will increase? Therefore, one must be impartial in restraining the wicked, like Zhang Yong 張詠 in his strictness and clear decisiveness; then by overawing a single person, tens of thousands will submit, …

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
蜀民之惡可去矣公於撫善若張詠之公平信
義則將撫一人而千萬人勸蜀民之善可復矣
此可見務其實者必得其效徒徇其名者又何
效之可臻哉愚也生於斯長於斯其於古今治
蜀之事略陳其梗槩矣儻得膺民社之寄而竊
一命之榮則豈無所取法哉敢以是復
明問顧恕其狂斐而進教之幸甚
punctuated: 蜀民之惡可去矣。公於撫善，若張詠之公平信義，則將撫一人而千萬人勸，蜀民之善可復矣。此可見務其實者必得其效，徒徇其名者又何效之可臻哉！愚也生於斯，長於斯，其於古今治蜀之事，略陳其梗槩矣。儻得膺民社之寄，而竊一命之榮，則豈無所取法哉？敢以是復明問，顧恕其狂斐而進教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …and the wickedness of the people of Shu (Sichuan) can be eliminated. If one is impartial in comforting the good, like Zhang Yong 張詠 in his fairness, trustworthiness, and righteousness, then comforting a single person will encourage tens of thousands, and the goodness of the people of Shu can be restored. From this it can be seen that those who attend to substantive reality will surely achieve results, whereas how can those who merely pursue the name attain any results at all? In my foolishness, I was born here and grew up here, and regarding the affairs of governing Shu in ancient and modern times, I have roughly set forth their general outline. Should I be fortunate enough to receive a charge over the people and the altars of the soil and grain, and humbly obtain the honor of a first official appointment, how could I lack models to emulate? I venture to offer this in reply to your illustrious question; if you would kindly pardon my rash and unpolished words and grant me further instruction, I would be most fortunate.

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試小錄後序
聖天子改元之初適當開科取士四川
藩臬重臣恭循禮典幣聘儒官以
司考較〔禎〕叨預其列協心秉公務
精去取以副
朝廷求賢圖治之盛心凡三試道藝
文言得中式者七十人遵
===
定制也小錄既成僉謂〔禎〕宜序于後
稽諸先王之世教民以德行道藝
而賓興之故士皆謹其言行脩己
以俟之蚤夜孜孜惟慮德業之弗
脩不憂爵祿之未至夫子所謂言
寡尤行寡悔祿在其中孟子所謂
脩其天爵而人爵從之者是已洪
punctuated:
四川鄉試小錄後序

聖天子改元之初，適當開科取士。四川藩臬重臣恭循禮典，幣聘儒官以司考較。〔禎〕叨預其列，協心秉公，務精去取，以副朝廷求賢圖治之盛心。凡三試道藝文言，得中式者七十人，遵定制也。小錄既成，僉謂〔禎〕宜序于後。

稽諸先王之世，教民以德行、道藝而賓興之。故士皆謹其言行，脩己以俟之，蚤夜孜孜，惟慮德業之弗脩，不憂爵祿之未至。夫子所謂「言寡尤，行寡悔，祿在其中」，孟子所謂「脩其天爵而人爵從之」者，是已。洪
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

At the beginning of the new reign era of the Sage Son of Heaven, the time was right to open the examinations and select scholars. The senior officials of the Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission of Sichuan respectfully followed the ritual regulations and sent gifts to invite Confucian officials to take charge of the grading and evaluation. I, [Zhen], had the undeserved honor of being included among their ranks. Working in harmony and upholding impartiality, we strove for precision in accepting and rejecting candidates so as to fulfill the Court's grand intention of seeking out the worthy and planning for good governance. In all, across three sessions testing their mastery of the Way, the arts, and literary expression, we obtained seventy men who met the standard, in compliance with the established quota. Now that the examination record has been completed, everyone has said that I, [Zhen], ought to write a postface at the end.

Examining the age of the former kings, they taught the people moral conduct and the arts of the Way, and then recommended them as honored guests. Therefore, scholars were all careful in their words and deeds, cultivating themselves while awaiting their opportunity. Working diligently from morning to night, they worried only that their virtue and accomplishments were not cultivated, and did not fret that rank and emolument had not yet arrived. What the Master meant by "Make few mistakes in speech and have few regrets in action, and emolument is found therein," and what Mencius meant by "Cultivate the nobility of Heaven, and the nobility of men will follow it," is precisely this. Humbly…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
惟我
朝
列聖相承法古為治每三歲舉行賔興
之典亦古人脩身謹行之遺意也
然非試以道藝則賢否何由而分
夫道藝者賔興賢能之根柢道以
文著藝以言宣文萃乎理言得於
===
心以之潤色
皇猷者此也以之爲詩事君此也以
之育德振民者亦此也推而至于
順天撡序創制立度靡事遺者
亦莫不由於此也然諸士子生逢
重熙累洽之世氣化醇厚之日涵養德
行優游道藝文表於行言合乎道
punctuated: 惟我朝列聖相承，法古為治，每三歲舉行賔興之典，亦古人脩身謹行之遺意也。然非試以道藝，則賢否何由而分？夫道藝者，賔興賢能之根柢。道以文著，藝以言宣，文萃乎理，言得於心。以之潤色皇猷者，此也；以之爲詩事君，此也；以之育德振民者，亦此也；推而至于順天撡序、創制立度，靡事遺者，亦莫不由於此也。然諸士子生逢重熙累洽之世、氣化醇厚之日，涵養德行，優游道藝，文表於行，言合乎道。
translation_en: …Having reverently considered that in our Dynasty a succession of Sacred Emperors have modeled their governance on antiquity, holding the ceremony of recommending worthy men as guests to the court every three years, this too embodies the enduring intention of the ancients in cultivating the self and being circumspect in conduct. Yet if candidates were not tested in the Way and the arts, how could the worthy and the unworthy be distinguished? Now, the Way and the arts are the very foundation for recommending the worthy and the capable. The Way is made manifest through literary composition, and the arts are expressed through words; literary composition gathers principle together, and words are attained within the mind. That by which one lends grace to the imperial plan is this; that by which one masters the Odes to serve one's ruler is this; that by which one nurtures virtue and rouses the people is also this; and extending even to according with Heaven and ordering the seasons [?], establishing institutions and setting up standards, leaving no affair neglected—there is none of these that does not stem from this. Now you scholars have been born into an era of acumulatively flourishing peace and a day when the transformative influences of thevital ether are pure and generous; you have nourished your moral conduct and immersed yourselves at leisure in the Way and the arts, so that your literary compositions give outward expression to your conduct and your words accord with the Way.…

title: 成化元年四川鄉試錄
text:
用是抱藝而來得雋而行又與天
下士角勝南宮敷對
大廷揚休稱制展釆錯事索耦皐伊
亦惟以道藝文言得之於心者措
之於行也豈徒托之空言哉脫若
靜言庸違隳名爽實則有玷於科
目而啓人之姍諷可不畏歟敢以
是規勉之
山東東昌府丘縣儒學教諭馮禎
謹序
punctuated:
用是抱藝而來，得雋而行。又與天下士角勝南宮，敷對大廷，揚休稱制，展釆錯事，索耦皐、伊，亦惟以道藝文言得之於心者，措之於行也。豈徒托之空言哉？脫若靜言庸違，隳名爽實，則有玷於科目，而啓人之姍諷，可不畏歟？敢以是規勉之。
山東東昌府丘縣儒學教諭馮禎謹序。
translation_en:
…Therefore, they come bearing their literary skills and depart having won distinction. Moreover, when they compete for supremacy with the scholars of the realm at the Southern Palace [the Ministry of Rites, i.e., the Metropolitan Examination], present their replies in the Great Court [the Palace Examination], extol imperial beneficence in response to the imperial decree, display their brilliance and carry out affairs, and seek to match Gao Yao and Yi Yin, it is only a matter of taking the moral Way, skills, literature, and words that they have grasped in their minds and putting them into practice in their conduct. How could this merely be entrusted to empty words? Should they speak smoothly when at rest yet act perversely when employed, ruining their reputations and failing the reality, they would bring blemish upon the examination system and invite the ridicule and satire of others—how could one not be fearful of this? I venture to offer these words as an admonition and encouragement to them.
Respectfully prefaced by Feng Zhen 馮禎, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qiu County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
